title: Politics: A Very Short Introduction
author: Kenneth Minogue
target_audience: General readers interested in political theory
Anyone seeking a foundational understanding of politics
core_themes: The role of the individual and society
primary_purpose: To provide a concise, accessible introduction to the foundational concepts, key debates, and enduring questions of politics as a field of study, helping readers grasp what politics is, why it matters, and how it shapes societies.

structure_format.organization: Thematic chapters that progressively deepen the analysis—from broad definitions to philosophical implications

key_concepts_lessons: Politics encompasses more than governmental affairs—it is about collective decision-making and who gets what, when, and how.
Political systems and ideologies profoundly shape societies and individual lives.
Freedom and order exist in tension, and politics is often about negotiating this balance.
Power and authority operate in visible (institutions) and invisible (norms, consent) forms.
Understanding politics requires critical engagement with competing perspectives.
Political ideas and arrangements are not static—they evolve in response to historical forces.
notable_features: Compact, accessible primer aimed at demystifying key concepts
Avoidance of jargon, making it friendly for beginners
Inclusion in the acclaimed ‘Very Short Introduction’ series
cultural_historical_context: Published at the turn of the 21st century, a time of increasing global interconnectedness and renewed debates about governance, democracy, and the role of the state after the Cold War era.
reception_impact: Widely used as an undergraduate and general interest introduction
Praised for its clarity and breadth in a brief format
Considered a model for multidisciplinary introductions within academia
Some critics see its brevity as a limitation for deeper inquiry
comparable_titles: Political Philosophy: A Very Short Introduction by David Miller
